source: read-only wireless ADB logcat of the owner's manual Settings > System update check at 08:30-08:31 local
method: observation only; nothing on the laptop was changed
finding: Google DID offer this device a system update. GMS SystemUpdate (com.google.android.gms .update.SystemUpdateActivity) found a candidate, fetched payload_metadata.bin into /data/ota_package, and asked the stock update_engine to validate it. The device rejected it before downloading or writing any system data; the UI briefly showed Preparing System for Update, then returned to up to date.
why_rejected: The metadata signature check passed (the payload is still signed by Google's key, and the laptop still carries Google's otacerts because the OpenBook certificate release is not on it yet).

The real stop was the source-partition content check: the offered update is an incremental (delta) that expects the exact stock system on disk. Our system carries the compatibility changes (Digitalis, trackpad fix, sleep fix), so the on-disk source hash did not match what the delta targets, and update_engine returned a source-hash-mismatch error during PreDownloadValidateAction.
The follow-on full-payload fetch returned HTTP 403.
boot_note: update_engine logged that boot_a is not in super metadata (expected on this single-slot device); it never reached partition writes.
implications: This hybrid DOES receive Google OTAs over the air; our earlier read of the public recovery manifest (still only 16452207) does not capture the Omaha server-side offer.
Right now the only thing stopping a Google OTA is the natural source-hash mismatch from our patches. That is fragile: a full (non-incremental) payload would not hit the source-hash check.

This is exactly why the OpenBook OTA-certificate release (RB-20261022-01, ANAL-253) should reach the laptop: it refuses a Google-signed payload at the first signature check, deterministically, before any staging.
It also confirms the capture step of the patch pipeline: the offered payload metadata and URL are visible in the log for an authorized, owner-driven adaptation flow.
redactions: update URL and any account/device identifiers are not recorded here
